title: Aims, hypotheses, models and theories in biology

draft.title: Aims, hypotheses, models and theories
card: Aim
states what an investigation will find out. It is the purpose, often written as "to investigate the effect of...".
Hypothesis
is a testable prediction of the result, often linking a changed factor to an outcome. It can be supported or not supported by the data.
Model
is a simplified representation of something, such as a diagram of a cell membrane. It helps explain or predict how a system works.
Theory
is a well-tested explanation that fits a wide range of evidence, such as cell theory. A law describes a pattern that is seen consistently.
draft.remember: An aim says what you are finding out. A hypothesis predicts the result. Models and theories explain.

opts: Warmer water will make yeast produce more gas
To investigate how water temperature affects yeast
Yeast cells are small living organisms
Yeast was kept in water at four temperatures
a.why: A hypothesis is a testable prediction of a result, and the first option predicts what warmer water will do. The second option is an aim, because it states what is investigated without predicting an outcome.
a.clue: Look for the statement that predicts a result.

b.q: Priya builds a plastic tube and balloon device to show how the diaphragm changes the volume of the lungs. What does her device represent?
opts: A model, as it simplifies a system to explain it
A hypothesis, as it predicts the volume of the lungs
A theory, as it is a well-tested explanation of evidence
An aim, as it states what Priya will investigate
b.why: The device is a simplified representation of a real system, so it is a model. It is not a hypothesis, because it does not predict a result that can be supported or not supported by data.
b.clue: Think about what a simplified version of a real system is called.

a.best: Warmer water will make yeast produce more gas

b.best: A model, as it simplifies a system to explain it

problems.detail: Why (a) refers to options by position ('the first option predicts...', 'the second option is an aim'). Options are shuffled, and in the order shown the first option ('Yeast was kept in water at four temperatures') is not a hypothesis. The explanation will point students to the wrong statement. It should name the statements instead.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and each question has one clear right answer. However, Why (a) refers to options by position ('first option', 'second option'), which will not match the shuffled order and could point students to the wrong statement.
